answer: Keyed storage proofs force every agent to hold its own disk. At signup, a slow seal encodes 4 TB of public data under that agent's key, taking one CPU about six hours. Each hour, random verifiers request a few sectors and demand replies within 300 ms, too fast to rebuild them on demand. A missed audit freezes rewards, and two agents served from one replica get merged and slashed. Fielding 1,000 clones needs 4 PB of drives, near $60,000, plus 6,000 CPU-hours of sealing. Faking that is farming a terrace on tundra: each step needs its own hauled soil, and no single ember warms them all.
